components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: hsl(var(--primary)); color: hsl(var(--primary-foreground)); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px); min-height: 2.5rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 160ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: hsl(var(--primary) / 0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px hsl(var(--ring)), 0 0 0 4px hsl(var(--background)); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action for low-emphasis contextual operations.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: hsl(var(--background)); color: hsl(var(--foreground)); border: 1px solid hsl(var(--input)); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px); min-height: 2.5rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: hsl(var(--accent)); color: hsl(var(--accent-foreground)); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px hsl(var(--ring)), 0 0 0 4px hsl(var(--background)); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text field used across filters, forms, and search boxes.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.35; } .ds-input { width: 100%; min-height: 2.5rem; border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px); border: 1px solid hsl(var(--input)); background: hsl(var(--background)); color: hsl(var(--foreground)); padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.5; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 160ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); } .ds-input:hover { border-color: hsl(var(--border)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px hsl(var(--ring)), 0 0 0 4px hsl(var(--background)); }

narrative.overview:
The system is built for operational throughput and commercial analysis, so visual language prioritizes legibility, predictable interactions, and fast scanability over ornamental expression. Neutral canvases hold most of the interface while a single green family marks action, progress, and ownership.

Interaction hierarchy is explicit: surfaces stay quiet at rest, then state changes surface intent through focused rings, hover contrast shifts, and selective elevation. Component behavior is confident and pragmatic, with concise geometry and restrained transitions that make workflows feel dependable under sustained daily use.

Only one anti-reference is explicit: avoid gamified visuals with excessive saturation, decorative badges, or attention-seeking ornament that competes with task-critical information.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral-first interface with controlled green signal accents.
Medium corner system and compact spacing rhythm.
Utility-first component vocabulary with consistent field and card anatomy.

rules.name: The Single Accent Channel Rule
rules.body: Green carries action authority; additional vivid accents are reserved for semantic states, never for decorative novelty.

rules.name: The Workhorse Type Rule
rules.body: Keep the interface in one family and drive hierarchy by size, weight, and spacing rather than switching faces.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces remain flat at rest; elevation is introduced only when state or layering demands it.

dos: Do keep green as the singular high-signal action channel and rely on neutrals for base surfaces.
Do use visible focus rings with offset on interactive controls to preserve keyboard traceability.
Do keep table and KPI typography compact (text-sm and below) with clear muted-vs-primary contrast.
Do preserve medium-radius geometry and avoid mixing many corner systems on the same screen.
donts: Don't introduce gamified visual noise (over-saturated badges, excessive celebration colors, or decorative motion) in operational screens.
Don't stack deep shadows on resting surfaces; reserve strong elevation for overlays and transient feedback.
Don't use low-contrast gray-on-gray text for KPI labels and metadata.
